profile.org_note: Single-market, founder-controlled company run from one Dallas office (500 Crescent Court, Suite 350). The 2026 Texas Comptroller record lists Randall Van Wolfswinkel as the only officer and director (President, Director); Keith Hardesty is the Division President and the company's registered agent. No land, finance or treasury executive is named anywhere public, so land and capital decisions most likely sit with the owner and Hardesty (inferred).
profile.summary: Conventional private for-sale homebuilder, locally owned, incorporated in Texas in January 1986 and building only in Dallas-Fort Worth under three brands (First Texas Homes, luxury Gallery Custom Homes, boutique Harwood Homes). Its site lists 48 communities in 31 DFW cities. It both buys finished lots in third-party master plans and develops its own land (it bought a 132-acre, 490-lot pod in Legacy Hills, Celina for cash in 2021), which makes it a plausible land-banking customer, though no land banker or lender is publicly linked to it. A Houston operation mentioned in some third-party profiles does not appear on the company site today.

gaps: Head of land acquisition / land development: not publicly disclosed. No land title of any kind was found for this company on its site, in state records or in the directories opened.
CFO, controller, treasurer or any finance head: not publicly disclosed.
The company website names no executives at all; every name here comes from state records or third-party directories.

Founder and owner status of Randall Van Wolfswinkel: seen only in search snippets (Forbes 2020, The Real Deal 2023, Dallas Morning News 2010 pages would not open). The state record confirms he is the sole officer and director.
Keith Hardesty's exact current title: Division President (BBB, RocketReach) versus CEO (2026 Builder 100 listing, snippet only). The Builder page returned 403 and could not be opened.

Houston: the orchestrator lead and one auto-generated third-party profile mention a Houston division, but the company site lists only Dallas-Fort Worth communities today. The 'Blake Roberts, President, Houston Division' claim in that profile is wrong: HousingWire (2026-04-21) shows his career as Camillo Properties, Century Communities and now Glenview Homes, with no First Texas role. Whether First Texas ever built in Houston was not confirmed.
Email pattern: not publicly confirmed. Published addresses are generic only (onlineconcierge@firsttexashomes.com, info@firsttexashomes.com).
Direct phone numbers for executives: not published.

The swarm's shared web-search allowance ran out part-way through this builder, so city council / planning minutes and local-press searches for a land signatory were not completed. A follow-up pass with search (plat owner certificates, PID documents in Celina, Anna, Forney, Midlothian) is the most likely way to surface a land contact.
